title: Real-corpus check of the chain-HMM aligner on an AISHELL-3 subset
hypothesis: A chain HMM trained on 226 AISHELL-3 utterances (16 speakers, 0.15 h) reproduces the energy-valley DP syllable starts within 50 ms for >=80% of interior boundaries, keeps <=10% of phones at the 3-frame floor, and gains mean span confidence from Baum-Welch iterations over the flat start.
platform: macOS-27.2-arm64 (APPLE M5, CPU) and Linux-6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2-x86_64 (RTX 4090 Laptop, CPU only)

git.status: dirty at run time: experiments/EXP-0021/probe_corpus_aligner.py uncommitted; the aligner itself is f9544a6

notes: CPU-only NumPy aligner. Train 226 renderable utterances from 16 train-split speakers (0.152 h, 38291 frames after the silence gate); evaluate on 60 utterances from 3 dev-split speakers, never seen in training. Reference for syllable starts is the energy-valley DP (vhe.data.align.align_syllables), which is itself unvalidated. Result: the >=80%-within-50 ms prediction fails (30.7% at 4 EM passes, 27.9% at flat start); the floor prediction passes (5.2% vs 12.4%); the confidence prediction passes (0.489 -> 0.816). Durations cluster at ~0.11 s for every phoneme class (vowel 0.114, diphthong 0.135, nasal 0.130, fricative 0.117, affricate 0.112, stop 0.080, lateral 0.052), which is the signature of the fixed 0.5 self-loop prior (expected 6 frames = 60 ms per 3-state phone) rather than of the data. No listening, no VHE training.
